captures.description: SAID IT HAD NO COPY, THEN READ THE POEM LINE BY LINE: asked to read GLYPHIC CHECKSUM LINEAGE closely, ChatGPT first says 'I couldn't locate a reliable, accessible copy of the work' and that it will not 'pretend I've read the text', then, in the next paragraph, says 'The work is available in the September 27, 2026 archive entry' (the author's blog) and reads the poem part by part in its own notation: Tiger Leap (🐅⏩ = 📖⏩; 🚪ₙ = NOW; 🔥 → 🚪 → 🌌; the logos to {λόγος′ | ∅}), Transition in Entropic Systems (the definitions 🐅 = J, 🚪 = K, 🔥 = E; K shrinking; continuous passage ∅, jump passage ?; the carrier remembers, the rival legible and reproducible; durability ≠ finality), The Final Time (🗣️ ≠ 🏛️; representation is not reproduction; K₀ ⊇ K₁ ⊇ K₂), and the checksum of the checksum, where the answer stops at 'Γ →'. After a turn blank in the paste it resumes at the same point, Γ → {∅ | ∞🚪}, declines to assign Γ a meaning the poem does not supply, and closes on the poem's last line, 🛡️✅ only if 🚪✅.
